source.note: Scan without a text layer. Combined Senior Certificate / National Senior Certificate paper (cover and running header: SC/NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 11); PDF page n = printed page n. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.text_md: $x^{2}+10x+8=0$  (correct to TWO decimal places)

Solve simultaneously for $x$ and $y$:

$x+y=3$  and  $2x^{2}+4xy-y=15$
If $n$ is the largest integer for which $n^{200}<5^{300}$, determine the value of $n$.
$7\,;\,x\,;\,y\,;\,-11\,;\,\ldots$ is an arithmetic sequence. Determine the values of $x$ and $y$.
Determine the general term of the pattern in the form $T_{n}=an^{2}+bn+c$.
Calculate the value of the $50^{\text{th}}$ term of the pattern.
Show that the sum of the first $n$ first-differences of this pattern can be given by $S_{n}=6n^{2}+3n$.
How many consecutive first-differences were added to the first term of the quadratic number pattern to obtain a term in the quadratic number pattern that has a value of $21\,060$?
Prove that $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}4\cdot 3^{2-k}$ is a convergent geometric series. Show ALL your calculations.
If $\displaystyle\sum_{k=p}^{\infty}4\cdot 3^{2-k}=\dfrac{2}{9}$, determine the value of $p$.
Write down the equations of the asymptotes of $h$.
Determine the equation of the axis of symmetry of $h$ that has a negative gradient.
Sketch the graph of $h$, showing the asymptotes and the intercepts with the axes.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for sketching a hyperbola; tagged with fn.hyperbola-asymptotes and fn.intercepts.

questions.stem_md:
The graphs of $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{2}(x+5)^{2}-8$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{1}{2}x+\dfrac{9}{2}$ are sketched below.

* A is the turning point of $f$.
* The axis of symmetry of $f$ intersects the $x$-axis at E and the line $g$ at $\mathrm{D}(m\,;\,n)$.
* C is the $y$-intercept of $f$ and $g$.

questions.text_md: Write down the coordinates of A.
Write down the range of $f$.
Calculate the values of $m$ and $n$.
Calculate the area of OCDE.
questions.notes: Area of trapezium OCDE from the intercepts and D. No dedicated coordinate-area skill.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of $g^{-1}$, the inverse of $g$, in the form $y=\ldots$
If $h(x)=g^{-1}(x)+k$ is a tangent to $f$, determine the coordinates of the point of contact between $h$ and $f$.

questions.stem_md:
The graph of $f(x)=3^{-x}$ is sketched below. A is the $y$-intercept of $f$.
B is the point of intersection of $f$ and the line $y=9$.

questions.text_md: Write down the coordinates of A.
Determine the coordinates of B.
Write down the domain of $f^{-1}$.
Describe the translation from $f$ to $h(x)=\dfrac{27}{3^{x}}$.
Determine the values of $x$ for which $h(x)<1$.

questions.stem_md: On 31 January 2020, Tshepo made the first of his monthly deposits of R$1\,000$ into a savings account. He continues to make monthly deposits of R$1\,000$ at the end of each month up until 31 January 2032. The interest rate was fixed at $7,5\%$ p.a., compounded monthly.

questions.text_md: What will the investment be worth immediately after the last deposit?
If he makes no further payments but leaves the money in the account, how much money will be in the account on 31 January 2033?

Jim bought a new car for R$250\,000$. The value of the car depreciated at a rate of $22\%$ p.a. annually according to the reducing-balance method. After how many years will its book value be R$92\,537,64$?

questions.stem_md:
Mpho is granted a loan under the following conditions:

* The interest rate is $11,3\%$ p.a., compounded monthly.
* The period of the loan is $6$ years.
* The monthly repayment on the loan is R$1\,500$.
* Her first repayment is made one month after the loan is granted.

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of the loan.
How much interest will Mpho pay in total over the first $5$ years?
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for total interest paid on a loan; tagged with fin.outstanding-balance.

questions.text_md: Determine $f'(x)$ from first principles if $f(x)=2x^{2}-1$.
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\sqrt[5]{x^{2}}+x^{3}\right)$

questions.stem_md: The graph of $g(x)=ax^{3}+bx^{2}+cx$, a cubic function having a $y$-intercept of $0$, is drawn below. The $x$-coordinates of the turning points of $g$ are $-1$ and $2$.

questions.text_md: For which values of $x$ will $g$ increase?
Write down the $x$-coordinate of the point of inflection of $g$.
For which values of $x$ will $g$ be concave down?
If $g'(x)=-6x^{2}+6x+12$, determine the equation of $g$.
Determine the equation of the tangent to $g$ that has the maximum gradient. Write your answer in the form $y=mx+c$.

questions.stem_md:
A closed rectangular box has to be constructed as follows:

* Dimensions: length ($l$), width ($w$) and height ($h$).
* The length ($l$) of the base has to be $3$ times its width ($w$).
* The volume has to be $5$ m$^{3}$.

The material for the top and the bottom parts costs R$15$ per square metre and the material for the sides costs R$6$ per square metre.

questions.text_md: Show that the cost to construct the box can be calculated by: $\text{Cost}=90w^{2}+48wh$
Determine the width of the box such that the cost to build the box is a minimum.

questions.stem_md:
In a certain country, 10-digit telephone numbers with the following format were introduced:

Digits may be repeated.

questions.text_md: How many possible 10-digit telephone numbers could be formed?

questions.stem_md:
Certain restrictions were placed on the groups of digits:

* Area code: must be $3$ digits and the first digit can NOT be $0$ or $1$
* Exchange code: must be $3$ digits and the first and second digits can NOT be $0$ or $1$
* Number: must be $4$ digits and the first digit MUST be a $0$ or $1$

questions.text_md: How many valid 10-digit telephone numbers could be formed by applying the given restrictions?
Determine the probability that any randomly chosen 10-digit telephone number would be a valid phone number.

questions.stem_md: Harry shoots arrows at a target board. He has a $50\%$ chance of hitting the bull's eye on each shot.

questions.text_md: Calculate the probability that Harry will hit the bull's eye in his first shot and his second shot.
Calculate the probability that Harry will hit the bull's eye at least twice in his first three shots.
questions.notes: Binomial 'at least twice in three independent shots'; no dedicated binomial-probability skill, tagged with prob.tree-diagram.

questions.text_md: Glenda also has a $50\%$ chance of hitting the bull's eye on each shot. Harry and Glenda will take turns to shoot an arrow and the first person to hit the bull's eye will be the winner. Calculate the probability that the person who shoots first will be the winner of the challenge.

figures.caption: Parabola $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}(x+5)^{2}-8$ with turning point A, and line $g(x)=\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{9}{2}$ through C, the common $y$-intercept. The axis of symmetry of $f$ meets the $x$-axis at E and $g$ at $\mathrm{D}(m\,;\,n)$.
figures.notes: A(-5 ; -8) and D(-5 ; 2) follow from the given equations (asked in 4.2.1 and 4.2.3). Diagram not to scale.

figures.caption: Decreasing exponential graph of $f(x)=3^{-x}$, with $y$-intercept A and point B where $f$ meets the dashed line $y=9$.
figures.notes: The dashed horizontal line is y=9, labelled 9 at the y-axis. A(0 ; 1) and B(-2 ; 9) are asked in 5.1 and 5.2. Diagram not to scale.

figures.caption: Cubic $g(x)=ax^{3}+bx^{2}+cx$ through the origin, with turning points at $x=-1$ and $x=2$ marked by dashed vertical lines.
figures.notes: The equation g(x)=-2x^3+3x^2+12x follows from g'(x)=-6x^2+6x+12 and the y-intercept 0 (asked in 8.4). Turning-point x-coordinates -1 and 2 are given. Diagram not to scale.
